newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 36,600 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 46.281 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 16,500 tonnes, in the U.K. 10,000, in Denmark 6,000 and in Germany 4,100 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.382 million tonnes. This compares with the 69,000 tonnes awarded on January 17, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.508 million tonnes.

Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to be 46.281 Ecus per 100 kilos of sugar based on the Paris March contract -- the exact amount awarded -- and 46.198 Ecus based on May.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 40,000 and 90,000 tonnes versus 47,250 last week when the restitution was 46.302 Ecus.
